thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Smart-routing error spike for /v1/generate - region=europe-west1 - 5xx-rate 8.6% (baseline 0.4%) - rolling errors across multiple model variants. Pager: primary-oncall (marco-oncall). Alert details: https://alerts.example.internal/INC-4312
ryan.m: paging marco-oncall, seeing 502s and increased latency from europe users. customers complaining in #support.
marco-oncall: got it. looking into logs now. can someone paste the recent routing policy changes?
tess-sre: I pushed a small policy tweak 40m ago to prefer variant v2-quant for cost reasons in eu region. it should be a safe change but i'll attach the diff: ```diff
- fallback: [v1, v1-quant]
+ fallback: [v2-quant, v1]
```
ryan.m: that matches the spike start. v2-quant is newer; we saw a perf regression in long-context earlier but only in canary. maybe rollout leaked.
marco-oncall: I'm seeing a pattern: requests from eu hit v2-quant, KV cache keys are incompatible -> repeated misses -> requests trigger region fallback to us-central -> then routing policy sees us overloaded -> sends requests back to eu as "regional fallback" -> ends up in a loop between variants/regions with growing latency.
sara-oncall: can we force-route eu traffic to us-central as a quick mitigation? that reduces model mismatch maybe.
qa_lead: Support is reporting 120+ open sessions with 502s. impact flagged as P2 customer-facing.
devops: If we do a manual force-region, be aware of cached prefix KV entries. forcing region may cause hot keys to move and thrift a lot of cross-region traffic. proceed with caution.
marco-oncall: understood. options: 1) revert policy tweak (rollback) 2) force-route eu->us permanently 3) disable smart-routing for /v1/generate and send all traffic to dedicated pool (dedicated has compatible models). Which is fastest?
tess-sre: rollback is fastest (no infra change) but if caches already populated with v2-quant state, rollback could leave us with mixed state for a while. forcing route will be immediate but may spike egress. disabling smart-routing and switching to dedicated pool should be stable but requires token routing change and might need infra approval.
ryan.m: I'm leaning to disable smart-routing for the endpoint and send a controlled 10% canary to dedicated, then ramp. that keeps us from flip-flopping policies.
marco-oncall: agree. I'll execute the mitigation. executing command: ```infractl routing set-policy --service generate --policy fixed --target dedicated-pool-eu --reason "mitigate variant/regional fallback loop"```
marco-oncall: applied. starting 10% canary. watching metrics.
incident-bot: ACTION: routing policy change recorded by marco-oncall. Change ID: CHG-1179.
ryan.m: metrics: error-rate down to 3.1% in canary fraction, overall still 6.9% because old sessions. latency 95p also dropping for canary.
support-bot: new customer ticket from Acme Corp: "API 502s since 12:02, degraded throughput". tagging account as impacted.
marco-oncall: can we increase canary to 50%? if stable for 5 min.
tess-sre: i'm seeing increased cross-region egress after the force-route attempt earlier (someone did a manual override at 12:12). who ran a force command?
ryan.m: that was me, I tried a quick `infractl route --force-region eu->us` before we agreed on dedicated pool, thought it'd be a fast fix. sorry, I should have waited.
marco-oncall: that manual force created sticky connections and persisted some session routing in the LB, causing some requests to bounce back to eu and then to us and back. we have a small feedback loop.
devops: Undoing a force-region is not always immediate because of connection stickiness and KV TTLs. run `infractl connection drain --selector "route=force-eu-us"` and purge prefetched KV caches: ```bash
infractl connection drain --selector "route=force-eu-us" --timeout 60s
infractl cache purge --scope europe-west1 --prefix /kv/prefixes/generate
```
marco-oncall: running drain now. purging caches.
marco-oncall: drain done. cache purge started.
qa_lead: regression tests show a small uptick in token generation errors for sequences > 1024 while caches repopulate. tracking.
sara-oncall: good call to disable smart-routing. can we keep the dedicated pool until end of triage? we should avoid re-enabling until we have a proper compatibility check for quantized variants.
ryan.m: agreed. locking change: `infractl routing lock --service generate --reason "incident CHG-1179 - keep fixed routing until compatibility validation"`
incident-bot: LOCK applied by ryan.m. Lock ID: LOCK-903.
marco-oncall: update: overall 5xx down to 1.2% after cache purge and canary ramp to 50%. eu latency back near baseline.
support-bot: notified top 20 impacted customers with status update and ETA.
tess-sre: action item: add a preflight compatibility check to rollout pipeline to validate KV cache key formats between fallback candidates. also we need an automated safe-rollback that waits for active sessions to drain before flipping.
devops: action item: add `infractl route rollback --wait-for-sessions` flag.
ryan.m: handoff to sara-oncall for ongoing triage and postmortem creation. i'll update the incident doc with timeline.
sara-oncall: taking over. will produce RCA draft. notes so far: root cause = policy change preferring v2-quant in eu; contributing = manual force-region by ryan during triage, which caused sticky routing and a small region-variant fallback loop tied to KV incompatibility; mitigation = disable smart-routing + route to dedicated pool, cache purge, connection drain.
marco-oncall: thumbs up. :thumbsup:
qa_lead: i'll run expanded test matrix against v2-quant for long sequences and KV compatibility overnight.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitored. Incident page: https://incidents.example.internal/INC-4312.
sara-oncall: final note: we'll keep dedicated routing for 24h, then run staged rollout with compatibility checks. assigning follow-ups: @tess-sre (compat check), @devops (rollback-wait flag), @qa_lead (expanded tests), @ryan.m (postmortem timeline).
sara-oncall: handing off to next rotation at 20:00 UTC — all good for now. :white_check_mark:
